First, let's recall the product rule for logarithms:

$$
{log}_{n}⁡a+{log}_{n}⁡b={log}_{n}⁡(ab)
$$

Using the product rule, the given expression can be rewritten as

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{log}⁡(100{x}^{2})=\operatorname{log}⁡100+\operatorname{log}⁡({x}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Since $100={10}^{2},$ we have

$$
\operatorname{log}⁡100=\operatorname{log}⁡({10}^{2})=2.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{log}⁡(100{x}^{2}) & =\operatorname{log}⁡100+\operatorname{log}⁡({x}^{2}) \\  & =2+\operatorname{log}⁡({x}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$
